issues.description: Tab handling silently triggers fall-through accept logic for non-text keys
issues.detail: The guard `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` only short-circuits when Tab is pressed. Other keys that previously had distinct handling (Enter/Return, Escape, arrows) fall through to the new branch, which hides the popup and replays the event. This may suppress Escape/arrow navigation in the completion popup when the option is disabled.

issues.description: New branch placed before `item is None` guard, may forward events on empty popup
issues.detail: The new conditional runs before the `if item is None` fallback. If the popup is shown without items and the user presses any non-Tab key, the code now hides and forwards the event unconditionally. Previously, item normalization happened first. Verify this does not regress behavior when no completion item exists.

issues.description: No migration/default ensures existing users get `use_enter_for_completions` key
issues.detail: Adding a new key to DEFAULTS without bumping CONF_VERSION may leave existing users with stale completion config sections missing the key. `get_conf` should fall back to the default, but Spyder historically requires a version bump when adding keys to nested dicts. Confirm no KeyError on upgrade.

issues.description: Conf lookup on every keypress is wasteful
issues.detail: `self.get_conf('use_enter_for_completions', section='completions')` is called inside keyPressEvent for every key. This crosses the plugin config bus on each keystroke during completion. Consider caching the value via a config observer or reading once when the popup is shown.
`not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is harder to read than `not self.get_conf(...) and key != Qt.Key_Tab`. Minor style nit but improves clarity at a hot code path.

issues.description: No tests cover the new disable-Enter behavior
issues.detail: PR adds a user-facing toggle affecting an interactive editor path with no accompanying test. Given prior regressions around completion popup key handling in Spyder, a test verifying Enter falls through and Tab still accepts when the toggle is off would prevent future regressions.

review.summary: The PR adds a config toggle so Enter no longer accepts completions, leaving Tab as the only accept key. The core change is small but the keyPressEvent guard short-circuits on every non-Tab key, which risks regressing Escape, arrow, and empty-popup handling. The config key is added to DEFAULTS without an obvious version bump, and the new hot-path config lookup is uncached. No tests accompany the user-facing behavior change.
